text: The National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM) was founded on 22 September 1910 by Justo Sierra, aiming to create a secular, national university distinct from the outdated Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico. It merged and expanded Mexico City’s decentralized higher education institutions, initially uniting schools in Fine Arts, Business, Political Science, Jurisprudence, Engineering, Medicine, and Normal education, with Joaquín Eguía y Lis as its first rector. The university faced political challenges due to the Mexican Revolution and initial government control over curriculum and policies, leading to student strikes and resistance. In 1921, José Vasconcelos, rector, designed the university’s coat-of-arms featuring an eagle and condor surrounding a map of Latin America, with the motto "The Spirit shall speak for my people," symbolizing cultural and educational liberation. UNAM achieved autonomy in the early 1920s through student-led strikes and negotiations, ending its dependency on the Secretariat of Public Education. The university established its main campus, Ciudad Universitaria, in San Ángel, Mexico City, beginning construction in the 1950s and completed by 1954, later declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007. UNAM has grown into one of the world’s largest universities, with over 324,000 students, including those in its National Preparatory School and other national schools. It offers undergraduate and graduate programs across various schools, including Engineering, Law, Medicine, and the Arts, and operates a distance education system with over 32,000 students. UNAM is recognized globally for its research, particularly in Artificial Intelligence and robotics, and houses numerous research institutes such as the Institute of Astronomy, Biotechnology, and Nuclear Sciences. The university is also known for its strong political activism, cultural traditions like the Day of the Dead offerings, and its commitment to diversity, including initiatives for women in technology. Notable alumni and faculty include Nobel laureates Alfonso García Robles (Peace), Octavio Paz (Literature), and Mario Molina (Chemistry), as well as prominent politicians, scientists, artists, and business leaders like Carlos Slim and Andrés Manuel López Obrador. The university’s seal, motto, and imagery reflect its mission of cultural and educational empowerment for Mexico and Latin America.
